summary: Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
Yellava Subbarayalu is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served as a professor at Tamil University and worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).

Yeshe Thupten worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held a post at Middlebury College and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia. His students include Daniel Cozort, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Yeshi Dhonden was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director from 1961 to 1966, and taught students including Eliot Tokar.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2001) and has taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University. She founded the Woodenfish Foundation and served as department head and dean at the University of the West (~1996–2002).
Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. As of 2026, Zhang is attested as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1993–1999). He became an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2011.

Yijie Tang was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1947–1951). He later served as a professor there (~1980–2014) and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Yiliang Zhou was a historian, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, and Harvard University. A student of Yinke Chen (~1935–1939), he was a professor at Peking University (~1953–2001).

Ying-Kuang Chu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Bai Puren, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche. He taught Shek-Wing Tam and Yui Chi Lau.

Ying-shih Yü was a historian, philosopher, and sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard. He held professorships at Harvard (1969), Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton (1987–2001), and served as Pro Vice-Chancellor of The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1973–1975).

Yinggang Sun is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held a post at Fudan University (attested 2014) and serves as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yingshan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996) and is attested as an honorary research fellow there in 2026, having retired in 2023.

Yinke Chen was a sinologist, historian, and linguist who studied at institutions including Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard. He held major posts at Tsinghua University, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.

Yinshun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and earned a doctorate from Taisho University. He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association (1949–1952), and taught Cheng Yen.
Yirmiyahu Yovel was a philosophy scholar who studied at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong in 2013 under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University and Kyoto University (PhD), and served as a professor of philosophy, Buddhism, and Japanese poetry at the University of Haifa (~1978–2003).
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Takatsugu Hayashi. He is attested as an associate professor at Soka University in 2026.
